cases.title: Plane frame with beam span loads (static)
cases.source: AISC (1989) propped-cantilever tables (closed form); CSI ETABS Verification Example 1, Table 1-1
cases.tests: 2D frame statics, moment end releases, point + uniform span loads, station internal forces
assumptions: [derived] I = b h^3/12 from the printed member dimensions.
[assumed] Axial deformation neglected: A multiplied by 1e6.
Shear deformation off (SkyFrame default, no shear areas).
Pinned connections = moment releases at B1 end I and B2 end J; all bases fixed (immaterial for B1 under symmetric loads).
Live-load reduction off (never applied to analysis output).

cases.title: Three-story plane frame, rigid offsets, modes
cases.source: Closed-form 3-DOF eigen solution (Przemieniecki 1968; Paz 1985); CSI ETABS Verification Example 2, Table 2-1
cases.tests: 2D frame, rigid end offsets, modal analysis (RS blocked)
assumptions: [assumed] W14X90 I = 999 in4 (AISC; not printed).
[assumed] Axial deformation neglected: A x 1e6; beams rigid.
Shear deformation off (zero shear area in ETABS).
Mode shapes mass-normalised, sign aligned with the reference.
blocked: Table 2-2 (roof/2nd/1st RS displacements 2.139/1.716/0.955 in, C1 base moment 11,730 kip-in): needs the El Centro 1940 N-S 5 % spectrum ordinates, file ELCN-RS1 (ETABS install); not tabulated in the PDF.

cases.title: Three-story frame, UBC97 / ASCE 7-02 seismic and UBC97 wind
cases.source: Hand calculation from UBC 1997 / ASCE 7-02 formulas with the ETABS period; CSI ETABS Verification Example 3, Tables 3-1 .. 3-3
cases.tests: Code auto-lateral generators (UBC97 seismic, ASCE 7-02 ELF, UBC97 wind) and story shears
inputs: kip, in, s (run in kN, m)
Site C, Ss 1, S1 0.4, R 8, Ct 0.035, SUG I
100 mph, exp. B, I 1, Cq 0.8 / 0.5, width 20 ft
assumptions: [assumed] W14X90 AISC properties incl. shear area d tw (not printed); 24 in rigid offsets at the column tops as Example 2.
[derived] g = 386.09 in/s2 (SkyFrame and ETABS) vs 386.4 in the hand calculation: -0.08 % on every seismic shear.
[derived] Na = Nv = 1.0 (source B at 15 km) -> Ca 0.40, Cv 0.56.
[assumed] UBC97 wind: windward Ce at the level, leeward Ce at roof height, half-story tributary (convention not documented).
The SkyFrame modal period is passed as the program period.
differences: Example 3 seismic: -0.08 % is the gravity constant (386.09 vs 386.4 in/s2), identical to ETABS's own offset.

Example 3 wind: the UBC97 exposure / tributary convention behind the published forces is not documented and was not reproduced by any convention tried (level, integrated or mid-strip Ce; leeward at h or at z); SkyFrame's code-literal convention lands 2-4 % low.  Treat the wind rows as a convention gap, not a solver result.

cases.title: One-story 3D frame, torsionally coupled modes
cases.source: 3-DOF stiffness (Przemieniecki 1968) + eigen solution (Paz 1985); CSI ETABS Verification Example 4, Table 4-1
cases.tests: 3D frame, rigid diaphragm, rigid end offsets, torsionally coupled modal analysis, story mass from area weight
inputs: 15 ft, plan 30 x 30 ft, weight 150 psf
assumptions: [derived] Column layout read from Figure 4-1 (24 in columns on the -Y edge).
[derived] m = 135 k / 386.4 in/s2 = 0.34938 k-s2/in at the plan centre, Iz = m(a2+b2)/12.
[assumed] Axial deformation neglected (A x 1e6); beams rigid; column torsion neglected as in the 3x3 hand model.
Rigid offset 36 in at the column tops (flexible length 144 in).
Mode-shape sign aligned with the reference (arbitrary in any eigen solver); shapes are mass-normalised in both.

cases.title: Three-story 3D braced frame (L-plan), periods
cases.source: Wilson & Habibullah (1992) SAP90; Peterson (1981); CSI ETABS Verification Example 5, Table 5-1
cases.tests: 3D model from planar truss frames, axial-only members, rigid diaphragm with eccentric CM + MMI, modal (RS blocked)
inputs: A = 6 in2, E = 29,500 ksi, axial only
4 planar X-braced frames, 2 bays x 20 ft, 3 stories x 12 ft
assumptions: [derived] Frame line positions read from the plan (only the line coordinate matters under a rigid diaphragm).
[assumed] Pinned bases; axial-only = end moment releases; RX/RY inactive.
CM joint created by a massless in-plane stub.
blocked: Table 5-1 axial forces (column C1 story 1: 279.47, brace D1: 194.51, brace D3: 120.53 kip, W&H): need the El Centro 1940 N-S spectrum ordinates (ELCN-RS1, ETABS install); the PDF also does not state the modal combination, the number of modes or which frame is reported.

cases.title: Nine-story ten-bay plane frame eigenvalues
cases.source: Bathe & Wilson (1972); Wilson & Habibullah (1992) SAP90; CSI ETABS Verification Example 6, Table 6-1
cases.tests: Large 2D frame eigenvalue solution, tributary story mass, rigid floor
inputs: 3 kip-s2/ft per ft of member length
assumptions: [derived] Story mass 930 kip-s2/ft (levels 1-8), 765 (roof) by tributary length, as ETABS converts it.
Primary rows: ETABS mass model (one horizontal mass per floor, rigid floor).
Supplementary rows: the references' joint-lumped H + V mass without diaphragm.
[assumed] Shear deformation off (not mentioned).
differences: Example 6: the CSI comparison is between DIFFERENT mass models (story-lumped horizontal vs joint-lumped H+V); the +0.02 to +0.09 % gap of both ETABS and SkyFrame's ETABS-style model is that modelling difference, not solver error -- SkyFrame's reference-style model matches Bathe & Wilson to the printed digits.

cases.title: Seven-story plane frame, static lateral + modes
cases.source: Wilson & Habibullah (1992) SAP90; DYNAMIC/EASE2; CSI ETABS Verification Example 7, Tables 7-1 and 7-2
cases.tests: 2D frame, user sections, static lateral loads, 7 modes (RS and TH blocked)
inputs: 2 bays x 30 ft; 2 x 13.5 ft + 5 x 13 ft
assumptions: [assumed] E = 29,500 ksi and AISC A / I of the listed W shapes (not printed in the PDF).
[assumed] Rigid floor, no shear deformation, no end offsets; column strong axis in the frame plane.
differences: Example 7: the section properties CSI used are unpublished; with AISC values SkyFrame (like an independent numpy frame) lands ~0.05 % from the reference -- an input gap, not a solver gap.
blocked: Table 7-3 RS (roof 5.4314 in, C1 axial 261.50 k, C1 moment 9916.11 kip-in, W&H CQC): needs the El Centro spectrum ordinates (ELCN-RS1).
Table 7-4 TH maxima over 8 s (roof 5.48 in, base shear 284 k, C1 axial 258 k, moment 8740 kip-in, W&H): needs the ELCN-THU record (time step and format not in the PDF; TH damping not stated).
Exact section A / I and E (published only in the SAP90 manual / Example 07.EDB): AISC values reproduce the frame to ~0.05 %.

rows.quantity: Axial force, column C1 at ground

cases.title: Two-story 3D frame, eccentric mass, flat 0.4 g spectrum
cases.source: Wilson & Habibullah (1992) SAP90 [Ref. 1]; Peterson (1981) [Ref. 2]; CSI ETABS Verification Example 8, Table 8-1
cases.tests: 3D frame, rigid diaphragm with eccentric CM and no rotational mass, modal + flat-spectrum RS
inputs: 2 x 35 ft by 2 x 25 ft, 2 stories x 13 ft
6.212 kip-s2/ft per story at CM (38, 27) ft, no MMI
assumptions: [assumed] g = 32.2 ft/s2; X excitation; 5 % damping, CQC.
[assumed] J = I22 + I33 and nu = 0.3 (not printed; J only moves the 5th digit of T1).
CM joint created by a massless in-plane stub so the story mass sits at (38, 27) with zero rotational inertia.

cases.title: Shear walls: 6 configurations, 20 models
cases.source: CSI SAP2000 refined membrane/shell meshes (CSI 2002), as published in CSI ETABS Verification Example 15, Tables 15-1 .. 15-6
cases.tests: Shell walls (planar, on columns, coupled, C, thickened edges, E), rigid diaphragms, static lateral load
inputs: t = 12 in (a, b, c), 6 in (d, f), 8 / 18 in (e)
assumptions: Reference = CSI's SAP2000 refined-mesh column (CSI rule: only the finest mesh must meet the limits); the ETABS coarse-panel column is shown for comparison.
SkyFrame mesh: uniform 10 in elements; planar rows show the 20 in value in the note as a mesh check.

[derived] Planar walls: membrane shell type (ASDShellQ4). 3D walls: the published values identify the reference formulation (C wall = membrane only, E wall = full shell); each 3D row's note gives the other formulation's value.
[derived] 15b at the reference mesh (20 in, SAP2000 Fig. 15-9): the re-entrant column/wall corners are singular, so the value grows with refinement; the 10 in value is in the note.
[derived] 15c: equal lateral displacement on the pier floor joints only (named diaphragm); constraining the spandrel nodes makes the spandrel top chord axially rigid.

[assumed] 15c and 15e load magnitude 100 k (arrow unlabelled), +X at the top-left corner; 15c spandrels as 40 in shell bands; 15b first-story columns as 20 in thick shell legs; 15e piers as 18 in shell strips.
Rigid diaphragm at every floor (= SAP2000 equal-displacement constraint / rigid floor members).
Magnitudes compared (CSI tables print magnitudes); Z-rotation in rad.
differences: Example 15: ETABS's one/two-panel wall meshes under-predict the SAP2000 refined values by up to 21.6 % (1-story 120 in wall); CSI does not hold coarse meshes to the limits.  SkyFrame is run with a refined mesh, so it is compared with the refined reference.

Example 15d/15f: the reference element formulation is not stated; the C-wall values are reproduced only by membrane walls and the E-wall values only by full shells.  With the other formulation SkyFrame differs by: X-displacement, 6-story load X: shell: 0.7127 (-20.2 %); Z-rotation, 6-story load X: shell: 0.014078 (-26.3 %); Y-displacement, 6-story load Y: shell: 1.1835 (-0.4 %) | X-displacement, 6-story load X: membrane: 0.38284 (+4.7 %); Z-rotation, 6-story load X: membrane: 0.004279 (+9.7 %); Y-displacement, 6-story load Y: membrane: 0.75247 (+0.5 %).
Example 15b: re-entrant column/wall corners make the reference mesh-dependent; SkyFrame at the published SAP2000 mesh (20 in) matches it, finer meshes converge ~5-7 % softer (see the row notes).
cases.mesh: uniform 10 in quads (15b: 20 in = the reference mesh); planar: membrane ASDShellQ4; 3D: formulation matched to the reference

cases.title: Two-story 3D unsymmetrical frame, RS at 30 / 120 deg
cases.source: Wilson & Habibullah (1992) SAP90; Table 9-1 (6 periods, 2 CM displacements)
cases.tests: needs the ETABS installation files (Example .EDB models and El Centro / Loma Prieta records)
blocked: Story masses, mass moments of inertia and centre-of-mass coordinates (Figure 9-1 marks the CM but gives no value).
Response-spectrum ordinates, damping and modal / directional combination ("identical to Wilson and Habibullah (1992)", not reproduced).
Plan dimensions of B1 / B2 (only B3, B4, B5 carry 25 ft) and whether rigid offsets or self-mass are used.
Units of the two displacements (kip-ft model, presumably ft).
Available: E = 432,000 ksf, 18x18 in columns, 12x24 in beams, 2 stories of 12.5 ft -- the periods become checkable as soon as the masses are known.

cases.title: 3-story plane frame with ADAS hysteretic dampers, NLTH
cases.source: DRAIN-2DX; Table 10-1 (18 values, two damper sizes)
cases.tests: needs the ETABS installation files (Example .EDB models and El Centro / Loma Prieta records)
blocked: Column, beam and brace section properties ("user defined", values not printed).
ADAS (PLASTIC1) link stiffness, yield force, exponent and post-yield data per story ("manufacturer supplied").
Story masses, inherent damping and number of Ritz vectors.
El Centro 1940 N-S record file ELCN-THE (digitisation, dt, scale, duration).

cases.title: 3-story plane frame with viscous dampers, NLTH
cases.source: DRAIN-2DX; Table 11-1 (18 values, two damper sizes)
cases.tests: needs the ETABS installation files (Example .EDB models and El Centro / Loma Prieta records)
blocked: Column, beam and brace section properties.
Damper coefficient C per story and the damper link series stiffness k (alpha = 1 is given).
Story masses, inherent damping and number of Ritz vectors.
Record file ELCN-THE.

cases.title: Pounding of two planar frames (gap links), NLTH
cases.source: SAP2000; Table 12-1 (roof displacement, C1 axial force)
cases.tests: needs the ETABS installation files (Example .EDB models and El Centro / Loma Prieta records)
blocked: Gap link stiffness K and initial opening DI (Figure 12-1 shows the symbols only).
Spacing between column lines C3 and C4 (the gap span).
Story masses and the gravity loading behind the C1 axial force; damping; Ritz / modal count.
Record file ELCN-THU.
Section properties are "user defined" (W-shape weights from Figure 12-1 could be approximated with AISC values, as for Example 7).

cases.title: Base-isolated 2-story 3D frame (ISOLATOR1), NLTH
cases.source: SAP2000; Table 13-1 (C9 displacement, C1 axial force)
cases.tests: needs the ETABS installation files (Example .EDB models and El Centro / Loma Prieta records)
blocked: All ISOLATOR1 properties (K1, K2/K3, FY2/FY3, post-yield ratios, linear KE / DE).
Column and beam section sizes (only E = 3000 ksi and 150 pcf are given).
Loma Prieta records LP-TH0 / LP-TH90 (station, scale).
Damping, Ritz count, duration; which corner is removed at the 2nd level is not stated.

cases.title: Friction-pendulum base-isolated 3D frame (ISOLATOR2), NLTH
cases.source: SAP2000; Table 14-1 (C9 Uy displacement 4.2069 in, C1 axial force 38.25 kip)
cases.tests: needs the ETABS installation files (Example .EDB models and El Centro / Loma Prieta records)
blocked: Column and beam section sizes (only E = 3000 ksi, 150 pcf and the 8 in slabs are given).
Loma Prieta records LP-TH0 / LP-TH90.
Damping, Ritz count and duration; linear KE2/KE3, DE2/DE3 of the isolator.
Available: the full ISOLATOR2 nonlinear data (K1 1E3, K2/K3 1E2, mu 0.04 / 0.03, rate 20, R 60) and the plan geometry.

cases.title: P-Delta cantilever column (Timoshenko & Gere)
cases.source: Timoshenko & Gere, Theory of Elastic Stability, Sec. 1.11 (exact beam-column); CSI SAP2000 P-Delta cantilever test problem
cases.tests: Geometric nonlinearity: P-Delta case and ETABS-style model-wide P-Delta (iterative on loads)
inputs: L 10 m, 0.1 x 0.1 m, E 30 GPa
assumptions: Column meshed into 10 members (string-stiffness P-Delta needs a mesh; CSI recommends meshing).
Reference is the exact continuous beam-column; the residual of a chord-stiffness formulation on 10 segments is ~0.5 %.
differences: P-Delta: SkyFrame (like ETABS) uses the chord ('string') geometric stiffness; on a 10-segment column it is 0.48 % below the exact beam-column -- the formulation, reproduced to 1e-6 by an independent numpy assembly (tests/verification).

rows.quantity: Base moment H L + P delta
